service: Collagen implant injection for stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency
vignette: 63-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence (ICD-10-CM N39.3) using 4 pads daily. History and physical examination including a pelvic exam were completed. A simple cystometrogram showed normal bladder compliance and no abnormality of urethral support, and there is no urethral hypermobility on examination. An abdominal leak point pressure test with 200 cc in the bladder showed leakage at 72 cm H2O, establishing intrinsic sphincter deficiency. A collagen skin test was placed 5 weeks ago and evaluated over 4 weeks with no reaction. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. Periurethral collagen implant injection is requested; this would be her first session.
rationale_note: Female with ISD: no hypermobility, ALPP 72 cm H2O; skin test and trained urologist documented.

service: Collagen implant injection for stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency

Her urologist documents the prior success, the recurrence, a repeat history and physical examination including a pelvic exam confirming unchanged anatomy, and the medical justification for additional sessions. The injecting urologist is trained in cystoscopy and has completed a collagen implant training program. An additional collagen implant session is requested.
rationale_note: Exception: recurrence 9 months after successful collagen treatment, with documented medical justification for additional sessions.
